At Mina during his last Hajj, asked about rites done out of order, such as shaving before slaughtering, the Prophet said to do it now, for there is no harm.
Near the Jamra people asked about Hajj rites done out of order, and the Prophet told each to do it now, for there is no harm.
The Prophet and his companions reached Mecca on the fourth of Dhul Hijja intending Hajj, and he told those without sacrificial animals to assume ihram for Umra instead.
At the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet let a Khath'am woman perform the obligatory Hajj for her old father, who could not sit a mount, and turned Al-Fadl's face from her.
The Prophet and Anas made Hajj on a packsaddle and Aisha rode one to Umrah; after faith and jihad Hajj Mabrur is best, women's best jihad, wiping away sins.
Yemenis came for Hajj without provisions, saying they relied on Allah, and begged in Medina, so Allah revealed that they should take provision, the best provision being fear of Allah.
The Prophet prayed at Dhul-Hulaifa, went by Ash-Shajara and returned by Muarras, and was told Al-Aqiq is a blessed valley for prayer and Ihram of Hajj and Umrah.
In the Prophet's last Hajj, those with a sacrificial animal kept ihram until Hajj ended and others left it after Umrah; Ali and Abu Musa took his intention.
Hajj-at-Tamattu and Qiran: Ali kept to them despite Uthman, pre-Islamic people shunned Umrah in Hajj months, and those without a sacrificial animal left ihram, owing sacrifice or fasting.
Day of Nahr rites: no harm in changing their order, ihram kept until the sacrifice, the Prophet praying for those who shave before those who shorten, and Tawaf al-Ifada.
Asked at Mina on the Day of Nahr about shaving, slaughtering or stoning done out of order, the Prophet told each questioner: do it now, there is no harm.
On leaving Mina the Prophet prayed and slept at Al-Muhassab, a camping place rather than a rite, and Ibn Umar spent the night at Dhi-Tuwa on entering and leaving Mecca.
A pilgrim prevented from the Ka'bah slaughters the sacrifice, shaves and leaves ihram, as the Prophet did when Quraysh barred him at Hudaybiyyah, and as Ibn Umar intended.
Whoever performs Hajj without sexual relations or sin returns as sinless as a newborn child.
The Prophet let a woman perform Hajj for her dead mother, as one pays a debt, and a Khath'am woman for her father, too old to sit on a mount.
The Prophet sent Ibn Abbas from Muzdalifah to Mina at night; newly adult, he rode past the first row there; As-Sa'ib made Hajj with the Prophet aged seven.
At Dhul-Hulaifa in the valley of Al-Aqiq the Prophet is told in a dream it is a blessed valley, where he should pray and intend Umrah with Hajj.
In Ihram for Hajj at Mecca, companions were told to make it Umrah and leave Ihram; the Prophet, with his sacrificial animal, stayed in Ihram and shared it with Ali.
A man enlisted for a campaign whose wife is leaving for Hajj is told by the Prophet to go back and perform Hajj with her.
On the day of Nahr Abu Bakr has it announced that no pagan may perform Hajj after that year nor anyone circle the Ka'ba naked, throwing back the pagans' covenant.
Abu Musa, back from governing his people, took Ihram with the Prophet's intention but brought no sacrificial animal, so is told to do Tawaf and Sa'i and end Ihram.
Ali, back from Yemen, took Ihram with the Prophet's intention and is told to keep it, as they have sacrificial animals; those without one make their Ihram Umrah.
At the Hajj Abu Bakr led before the Farewell Hajj, it is announced that no pagan may make Hajj after that year and none may circle the Ka'bah naked.
At the Farewell Hajj those with sacrificial animals keep Ihram, others end it after Tawaf; menstruating Aisha does Umrah later; a daughter may perform Hajj for her frail father.
Safiya menstruates in the Farewell Hajj, but as she has already done Tawaf al-Ifada, the Prophet lets her set off.
Aisha says pilgrims took Ihram for Umrah, Hajj or both; the Prophet's was for Hajj, and those for Hajj or both kept it until the day of sacrifice.
At the Farewell Hajj the Prophet and some companions shave their heads, others cut their hair; Ibn Abbas's donkey passes the row at Mina; the Prophet combines Maghrib and Isha.
Verses of Hajj explained: the ransom for shaving the head when lice troubled Ka'b bin Ujra, Hajj at-Tamattu, trading in the Hajj season, and departing from Arafat with the people.
In the Hajj led by Abu Bakr, announcers and Ali proclaimed at Mina on the Day of Nahr: no pagan may perform Hajj, and none may circle the Ka'bah naked.
Leaving Mecca after Hajj, the Prophet found Safiyya sad at her tent; learning she had done Tawaf al-Ifada on the day of sacrifice, he said she could depart.
Asked on the Day of Nahr about rites done out of order, such as Tawaf before stoning or shaving before slaughter, the Prophet answered each, 'There is no harm'.
The Prophet wished he had not brought his sacrificial animal (Hadi), so he could end ihram with the people, whom he had told to use their ihram for Umrah.
Told of a mother who vowed Hajj but died, the Prophet bade her daughter perform it for her, as she would pay her debts, for Allah has more right.
The Prophet was told to pray in the blessed Aqiq valley and declare Umra and Hajj, fixed the miqats, and dreamt at Dhul-Hulaifa he was in a blessed valley.
Arriving for Hajj, the Prophet ordered the companions to end their ihram, making their wives lawful, saying he would too had he not brought the Hadi; they obeyed.
